subject: production-cutover: orphaned project quotas triggering request amplification
messages:
From: Elena Vargas <elena@medcore.health>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-20T08:42:00-08:00
Subject: Spikes + 5xx/429 after last-night cutover (urgent)

Hi Sean —

We started seeing large numbers of 429 + intermittent 5xx starting ~02:30 UTC after the cutover to the new org-routing yesterday. Our ingest pipeline is retrying aggressively and we’re seeing downstream timeouts. This is impacting clinical workflows in a few pilots.

Key symptoms: repeated 429s with X-RateLimit-Org header showing default-org, burst of retries that line up with our scheduled jobs, and two hours of elevated p50 latency.

Can you please escalate? We need an emergency mitigation plan (don’t care how — throttle us, put us on a fallback, anything short-term).

—Elena
Director, Platform Ops
MedCore Health
From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Elena Vargas <elena@medcore.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-20T09:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spikes + 5xx/429 after last-night cutover (urgent)

Elena —

Thanks for the flag and the symptom details. I’ve looped in Marissa (CS lead) and Ben (SRE). Short-term plan: we will (1) pause aggressive client-side retries via a transient inbound rule, (2) route MedCore’s requests to a dedicated fallback model pool, and (3) open an incident to map quota assignments.

Ben / Marissa — can you confirm we have capacity to move MedCore to a fallback pool and push a temporary per-customer throttle? I’ll own communication to the customer and exec ping if needed.

Sean
VP, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
From: ben_carter@redwood.ai
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-20T09:17:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spikes + 5xx/429 after last-night cutover (urgent)

Sean / Marissa —

Quick triage: initial logs show MedCore traffic flapping between two org ids after the cutover. A subset of their projects didn’t carry a project->org alias mapping, so requests are landing under the account that has very low project-level quotas (the "default-org"). That explains the sudden 429s plus bursty retries amplifying the load. Attached: quota-mapping-log.txt and early grafana screenshots.

Immediate mitigation I can push now (10–15m):
- Create a transient project alias so traffic maps correctly to MedCore org limits
- Apply a soft throttle to MedCore on the edge (limit steady QPS, allow short bursts)
- Temporarily route top customer routes to the fallback pool Sean mentioned

Longer-term: patch the aliasing job that runs in the cutover pipeline — there’s a race where projects created during the window are not inserted into the alias table. I’ll open INF-1298 and add a test to cover the race.

—Ben
SRE
From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai
To: Elena Vargas <elena@medcore.health>, sean.gallagher@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-20T09:36:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spikes + 5xx/429 after last-night cutover (urgent)

Elena —

We’re on it and I’ll send a short mutual action plan. For transparency: this looks like a quota-tier mapping gap from the cutover (not a deliberate throttle by Redwood). We’ll keep your production traffic prioritized while we patch.

Next steps (short):
- Ben to push alias and edge throttle (in-flight)
- Sean to confirm fallback routing and notify your execs of mitigation path
- I’ll coordinate with your security/compliance contacts once we stabilize to exchange audit logs

Expect a follow-up in ~30 minutes with status.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
To: Elena Vargas <elena@medcore.health>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, ben_carter@redwood.ai
Date: 2026-01-20T10:12:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spikes + 5xx/429 after last-night cutover (urgent)

Elena —

Quick update: Ben applied the project alias and we put a conservative soft throttle in front of your org. I’ve routed non-critical routes to the fallback pool; critical clinical routes remain on primary with prioritized capacity. You should see the retry amplification tail off within the next 10–20 minutes.

If you continue to see errors after 20 minutes, please reply with a sample request id and timestamp and we’ll hunt immediately.

Also scheduling an incident postmortem for Monday to review the cutover checklist and confirm the alias fix.

Sean
From: Elena Vargas <elena@medcore.health>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@medcore.health
Date: 2026-01-21T17:50:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Spikes + 5xx/429 after last-night cutover (urgent)

Sean / team —

Thanks for the rapid response and direct mitigations. The retry storm subsided after the alias push and throttle; latency returned to baseline. We’ll take part in the Monday postmortem — please include the quota-mapping logs and the list of org->project mismatches.

One ask for the postmortem: can you include an action item to ensure cutover runbooks explicitly validate alias insertion for any projects created in the migration window?

—Elena
Note: attachments referenced above: quota-mapping-log.txt (excerpt), support_runbook.pdf (runbook excerpt), grafana-spike-screenshots.zip. Forwarded headers preserved where applicable.
